findings.disposition_hint: the seven failing ids are listed in the reviewed manifest's outside_scope and each needs a coordinator decision, not a silent landing
findings.text: blocking: the landed reading turns seven committed tests red and the recorded gate runs none of them. gate/head-wait-targeted.log reports 7 failed and 137 passed at exit 1 at this head, while gate/base-wait-targeted.log reports 144 passed at exit 0 at 977adcb. The manifest's tests line runs only the new file plus tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py and tests/test_every_shared_home_lock_holds_across_nodes.py, so promotion reads green while the repository is red. The first of the seven is this line: a live probe at 1800 s with no declared horizon now reads wait_overdue False instead of True. That is the reading the plan's first clause asks for, and it contradicts the done_when's fourth clause, which requires the tests importing reckon.crew.recovery_liveness or reckon.crew.recovery_classification to add no failure against the base. The node cannot both land and satisfy its own measure. The repair is either a node granted those files to re-pin the overturned readings, or a narrowed exemption that keeps an alarm for a probe that never leaves a live state.

findings.disposition_hint: fold into a node that reads a cancelled job or a scheduler time limit, or exempt with the unbounded-wait risk recorded
findings.text: non-blocking: a live probe is exempted from the default horizon outright and no scheduler-known limit is read. _wait_expected_seconds at reckon/crew/recovery_wait.py:584 sources the horizon only from _WAIT_HORIZON_FIELDS, and nothing in reckon/crew reads a job's time limit, so the plan's scheduler-known limit becomes no limit at all while the probe reports a live state. A wait whose probe keeps printing RUNNING therefore has no clock, which is the reading the repository's own control at tests/test_a_wait_ages_on_its_stream.py:200 was written to prevent.

findings.disposition_hint: fold into a node that replaces the new helper with a call to the owner
findings.text: non-blocking: the function defined at this line duplicates the probe-answered capability owned by _the_probe_did_not_answer at reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:521. It reads the same structured answered flag, in a second module that the owner then imports, and the two disagree on a None observation: the owner treats None as not-unanswered, the new helper as not-answered. One fact therefore has two definitions in the classifier module.

findings.disposition_hint: exempted: recovery_wait.py is named in the plan's write paths but was not granted to this node, so extending the owner was fenced out; a repair node holding that file should make the new set a superset of the owner's
findings.text: non-blocking: the live-state set defined at this line forks the vocabulary the package already owns at reckon/crew/recovery_wait.py:1053, repeating running, pending and waiting as an unextended parallel set. A spelling added to the owner will not reach this reader, and a spelling added here will not reach the terminal-liveness refusal.
